cands.name: Chase Tramont
cands.bio: Republican incumbent, 46. Baptist pastor and marketing manager; former history teacher at Spruce Creek High School; Port Orange City Council 2016-2022. HD 30 since Nov 2022, re-elected 2024 with 66%.
cands.local_ties: Born in Daytona Beach in 1979; lives in Port Orange (Wikipedia).

record.text: Port Orange City Council 2016-2022; sponsored HB 391 (registered welfare system for parents of medically fragile children).

Voted for SB 484 (data centers), SB 300 (six-week abortion ban, 2023) and HB 991 (proof of citizenship); voted to place the property tax amendment on the ballot while saying he was not "a big fan" of it.

controversies.text: Wikipedia reports he has said the separation of church and state does not appear in the Constitution.

endorsements.text: Sen. Jason Brodeur and the Florida Police Benevolent Association endorsed him in 2022.

cands.gaps: Current donors not found. Owner-source check was limited: the alexjoneslive.com site search was run for this name and returned no results. stewpeters.com, rumble.com and infowars.com searches were blocked (HTTP 403) and the shared web-search quota was exhausted, so those were NOT checked.

votes.what: Joint resolution putting Amendment 3 (Save Our Homes property-tax changes: higher homestead exemption, lower assessment-increase limits) on the Nov 2026 ballot.
The 2025-26 General Appropriations Act (state budget), final vote.
Immigration enforcement bill from the 2025 special session: state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
Post-hurricane emergency management bill that also limits local governments' ability to adopt stricter development rules after storms.
Online Protections for Minors: restricts social media accounts for minors.
Interests of foreign countries: restricts land purchases near military sites and critical infrastructure by people from China and other 'countries of concern'.
Education: expands school voucher eligibility to all Florida K-12 students.
Heartbeat Protection Act: bans most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.
Public Safety: lets most adults carry a concealed firearm without a permit (permitless carry).
Property Insurance: creates the Florida Optional Reinsurance Assistance program (FORA) for insurers.
